Harvard Pilgrim Health Care  
Appeals Department

Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization  
Member: Cameron Jennings  
Member ID: W156639675  
Reference number: POC-79A305E63C-48045  
Requested service: ACL reconstruction  
CPT: 29888  
Date of denial: August 18, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Harvard Pilgrim’s denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The MRI and the rest of the clinical record support the requested procedure.

The June 11, 2026 MRI documents a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone-bruise pattern. It also shows intact menisci and no significant arthritis. This is a structural ACL injury that corresponds directly to the requested arthroscopic ACL reconstruction.

The imaging findings are also consistent with my clinical symptoms and examination:

- I have had 12 months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I have recurrent instability with pivoting and have given way twice on stairs.
- Provocative testing is positive on the affected side.
- Range of motion is limited by pain.
- The MRI confirms a complete ACL tear rather than showing an isolated pain condition or significant degenerative arthritis.

I have also completed extensive conservative treatment without adequate improvement. I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, from April 19, 2026 through July 12, 2026, for a total of 20 visits. I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on June 9, 2026 produced only three weeks of partial relief. Despite these measures, I continue to have pain and functional instability.

The record does not identify an active infection or untreated substance-use condition that would prevent surgery. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker. The procedure was requested by Marchetti, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, based on the documented complete ACL tear, persistent instability, failed conservative treatment, and objective examination findings.

Harvard Pilgrim’s publicly available prior-authorization page identifies InterQual Criteria as the commercial prior-authorization medical-review criteria source. The publicly available materials do not provide the ACL-specific criteria applied to this request, and I have not quoted or reconstructed those criteria here. Please identify the specific criterion or criteria that Harvard Pilgrim believes were not satisfied, provide the version or date of the criteria used, and provide the complete clinical rationale for the denial.

Please conduct a full reconsideration of the request using the MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and orthopedic assessment. Based on the complete ACL tear, recurrent instability, persistent symptoms, failed conservative care, and absence of significant arthritis, I request that Harvard Pilgrim overturn the denial and authorize ACL reconstruction under CPT 29888.

Please treat this as a timely standard appeal received within 180 days of the August 18, 2026 denial date. Please send the appeal determination and the specific clinical criteria applied to me in writing.

Sincerely,

Cameron Jennings
